{{Short description|Chinese mathematician}}

'''Zhiren Wang''' (Chinese: 王之任) is a Chinese mathematician, specializing in [[dynamical systems]]. He is known for his contributions to the [[rigidity (mathematics)|rigidity theory]] of [[group action]]s.<ref name=":0" />

== Education ==

Wang received his undergraduate education at [[Fudan University]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Math professor awarded Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems {{!}} Eberly College of Science |url=https://science.psu.edu/news/math-professor-awarded-brin-prize-dynamical-systems |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=science.psu.edu}}</ref> earning a B.S. in Mathematics (2004). He then pursued graduate studies in France, obtaining an [[Ingénieur]] degree from [[École Polytechnique]] and a [[Higher education in France|DEA]] (Diplôme d'études approfondies) in Mathematics from [[Paris-Sud University]] ([[Paris-Saclay University|Orsay]]) (both in 2006).<ref name=":1" /> He completed his Ph.D. in Mathematics at [[Princeton University]] in 2011 under the supervision of [[Elon Lindenstrauss]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zhiren Wang - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=210697#:~:text=MathSciNet,Advisor%201:%20Elon%20Lindenstrauss |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref>

== Career ==

After completing his doctorate, Wang held a postdoctoral fellowship at the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]], followed by a position as Gibbs Assistant Professor at [[Yale University]] from 2011 to 2014, and then faculty positions at [[Pennsylvania State University]] from 2014<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-12-09 |title=Zhiren Wang - Scholars {{!}} Institute for Advanced Study |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/zhiren-wang |access-date=2025-09-27 |website=www.ias.edu |language=en}}</ref> to 2025. In 2025, he moved to [[Johns Hopkins University]] as Professor.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://mathematics.jhu.edu/directory/zhiren-wang/ |title=Zhiren Wang |website=Johns Hopkins University Department of Mathematics |access-date=2024-12-19}}</ref> He has also held a [[Von Neumann Fellowship]] at the Institute for Advanced Study.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/zhiren-wang |title=Zhiren Wang |website=Institute for Advanced Study |date=9 December 2019 |access-date=2024-12-19}}</ref>

== Research ==

Wang's research focuses on several interconnected areas of mathematics: [[Dynamical system]]s, classification of [[group action]]s and [[Diophantine approximation]] and [[geometry of numbers]]. His work has made contributions to [[rigidity (mathematics)|rigidity theory]] in dynamical systems. In 2022, Wang received the [[Michael Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems]]<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Math professor awarded Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems {{!}} Penn State University |url=https://www.psu.edu/news/eberly-college-science/story/math-professor-awarded-brin-prize-dynamical-systems |access-date=2025-09-26 |website=www.psu.edu}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Spatzier |first=Ralf |date=August 19, 2024 |title=ON THE WORK OF ZHIREN WANG ON RIGIDITY IN DYNAMICS |url=https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/spatzier/wp-content/uploads/sites/1081/2025/06/ZHIREN_BrinPrize_FINAL-4.pdf}}</ref> for his "fundamental contributions to the study of topological and measure rigidity of higher rank actions, and his proof of Möbius disjointness for several classes of dynamical systems."<ref>{{cite journal |title=Mathematics People |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=69 |number=7 |pages=1248 |year=2022 |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202207/rnoti-p1247.pdf}}</ref>
